💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that arc Raiders has received a fresh upgrade today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks.
  • Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the upcoming “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.
  • According to recent reports, that, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance problems with some of the game’s weapons and tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that arc Raiders has received a fresh upgrade today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the upcoming “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

According to recent reports, that, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance problems with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark said pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

According to recent reports, in today’s update, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

Another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

According to recent reports, the patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

Beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

This change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

It has been revealed that check the official blog for the full change log for patch 1.3.0. If you’re just getting started with the hottest extraction shooter ever, our Arc Raiders tips offer plenty of help. You should also learn what all the different Map Conditions do in Arc Raiders, and how to best make use of each of them.

The C-HR is a smaller, sportier crossover SUV, while the bZ Woodland adds a larger, more rugged option.

Toyota is right now offering a deal on the 2026 bZ Woodland for Black Friday that might be worth a look.

The deal includes 0% APR financing for 72 months, plus an extra $1,000 Holiday Bonus Cash. Toyota noted that if you finance a newly introduced 2026 bZ Woodland for 72 payments, it will cost $13.89 for every $1,000 financed.

Industry observers note that toyota is promoting 2026 bZ Woodland leases as low as $449 a month. That’s also for a 36-month lease with $4,448 due at signing.

The Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower, which is 37 hp more than the standard bZ SUV with AWD.

Sources indicate that toyota’s standard bZ is offered with FWD and AWD powertrains. FWD models deliver either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models produce a combined 338 hp.

The Woodland model is also 6″ longer than the standard bZ, opening up an additional 30 cubic feet of cargo space on the inside.

Toyota’s bigger SUV also adds a rugged look and off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and up to 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Other rugged upgrades are standard, including All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.

Inside, both come with a 7″ digital cluster and a large 14″ touchscreen running the latest Toyota Audio Multimedia system with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

It has been revealed that although it uses the same 74.7-kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland version offers slightly less driving range because of the added power and off-road equipment. The 2027 bZ Woodland has an estimated range of up to 281 miles with all-season tires, or 260 miles with the optional all-terrain tires.

In comparison, the bZ is available with two battery packs: 57.7 kWh and 74.7 kWh. The base XLE FWD uses the 57.7 kWh battery, while the XLE AWD and FWD Plus, Limited AWD, and FWD models use the 74.7 kWh battery.

The standard 57.7 kWh battery provides an EPA range of up to 236 miles, while the 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 314 miles for FWD and 288 miles for AWD.

Sources indicate that both the bZ and bZ Woodland have a native NACS port, so drivers can use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. It takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

Scout Motors starts validation builds at $2B SC plant, deliveries in 2028

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars.
  • That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the firm was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.
  • According to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars. Scout confirms the first deliveries of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup won’t happen until 2028.

That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the firm was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.

According to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed. The Body Shop, Paint Shop, and Assembly Shop are all being used for the first validation builds.

It has been revealed that the Body Shop is the most automated part of the plant. Scout notes more than 750 robots join roughly 160 parts into each body, laying down about 5,000 weld points per vehicle, with AI-supported weld monitoring and a metrology system checking the results. At full capacity, the shop is designed to handle about 40 vehicles per hour.

Bodies then go through an electrified paint shop before landing in final assembly, where they’re married to the chassis and get their wiring, glass, seats, and wheels.

CEO Scott Keogh is clearly happy to have something physical to point to, saying that “what we are building in Blythewood is no longer a promise on paper.”.

Recent findings suggest that scout also shared photos of a Terra pickup and a Traveler parked inside the plant. Its own fine print notes that they show “concept and validation vehicles” with optional features, so don’t read too much into what’s on display:.

In a recent development, fair enough. But Scout is also careful about what this stage is. Teams are confirming the equipment is installed and works, and checking engineering, buildability, and parts maturity. Process validation and scaling up to production speed come later. Validation builds will continue “into 2027,” followed by pre-production builds, and then customer deliveries in 2028.

The company notes the plant will create more than 4,000 jobs, and it’s spending another $300 million on an onsite supplier park expected to support about 1,000 supplier jobs.

Industry observers note that when Keogh laid out the blueprint in late 2023, Scout remarked it would start production in 2026 with deliveries shortly after. That was still the target when Scout broke ground in Blythewood in February 2024.

According to recent reports, by the Traveler and Terra unveiling in October 2024, production had moved to 2027. Keogh then remarked in March that he expects the first customer to get a vehicle “sometime in 2028,” and that’s now the official line in Scout’s own press materials.

It has been revealed that it might not even be the end of it. Industry forecaster AutoForecast Solutions has the Traveler starting production in September 2028 and the Terra in March 2030. Scout hasn’t confirmed those dates, but it hasn’t given more precise ones either.

Recent findings suggest that the product itself has also changed under the hood. Scout rolled out as a pure EV brand, then added the “Harvester” range-extender option at the reveal. According to Keogh, Scout has more than 160,000 reservations, and 87% of them are for the gas-generator version. Those are $100 refundable reservations, not orders.

Der Spiegel reported earlier this year that integrating the range extender, which wasn’t part of the original plan, was among the technical problems pushing the timeline back.

For comparison, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and delivered the first ones four years later, a delay that was widely mocked. Scout is now on a similar four-year path from reveal to customer, and that’s for the SUV it’s launching first.

Recent findings suggest that A working body shop with 750 robots isn’t vaporware. Scout has a real factory, a real workforce, and two vehicles that people clearly want. 160,000 reservations is a big number for a brand that hasn’t sold a single vehicle in 46 years.

In a recent development, but validation builds are an early step, not a finish line. Scout still has to go through pre-production, prove its processes, and ramp to rate, and every one of those stages is where fresh automakers usually lose time. Rivian and Lucid both learned that the hard way.

According to recent reports, september 28? So we're 23 months away? I'm surprised the validation build yadda yadda stuff is supposed to take so long. It's not like VW doesn't know how to do this stuff, and that's a lot of money and equipment to sit mostly idle while 180,000 reservations holders are waiting for their cars. Maybe they're waiting for the market to change or are considering a whole other brand or product line?

It has been revealed that and the market Scout was designed for in 2022 no longer exists. The EV tax credit is gone, and most of Scout’s own reservation holders picked the gas generator. In the US, the range-extender market is still early, unlike in China, where they are already popular.

It has been revealed that but by 2028, Ford, Ram, and Jeep all plan to have range-extended trucks and SUVs on sale. Scout’s main advantage was being early with a cool, rugged, American-built electric truck. That advantage shrinks every quarter.

We’re still rooting for these vehicles. The Traveler and Terra are among the best-looking designs in the segment. But a $100 reservation is easy to walk away from, and the question is how many of those 160,000 people are still waiting in 2028.

#63915. Latest Update: Is Your Obsession Actually Limerence?

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (693 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Is Your Obsession Actually Limerence?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (693 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • It has been revealed that the experience and expression of human attachment is complex, to say the least.
  • Are you someone who obsesses about others?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

It has been revealed that the experience and expression of human attachment is complex, to say the least. As humans, we may share a universal ingrained wiring for connection, but how we navigate this interpersonal world is not the same from person to person.

Are you someone who obsesses about others? Maybe you understand infatuation in the early stages of love, but then know how to transition to a mutual relationship or let go? Forming steady and stable connections is easy for some people; others are tortured with intense and uncertain attachments. Fresh research provides insight into limerence, a specific form of intense attachment that is starting to gain more attention.

It has been revealed that imagine someone fixating on another person. This isn't hard to do. We hear about it on podcasts, watch it unfold in fantastic crime dramas, and, of course, some of us experience it in real life. From infatuation to unrequited love, examples of preoccupations with another person, outside of established relationships, color the romantic landscape. Limerence, however, is different.

Industry observers note that limerence is an intense and highly disruptive cognitive and emotional experience (Marshall et al., 2025; Tennov, 1979). Individuals in the throes of limerence are overwhelmed by the desire to be viewed positively by a specific someone else (i.e., the limerence object). This obsession manifests as uncontrollable rumination to the point that it interferes with day-to-day life.

Industry observers note that limerence is typically expressed toward someone with whom the experiencer is highly unlikely to form a real relationship. On the surface, this might seem like unrequited love, but it is far more intense and generally less realistic.

From a case study analysis, Wyant (2021) offered the following pathway by which people might come to experience limerence:.

A recent review (Bradbury et al., 2025) summarized a step-wise sequence proposed by Verhulst (1984). This model suggests that limerence begins in the context of need: a person's needs for emotional intimacy, support, and connection are not fulfilled in their current relationships. Limerence can follow from there:.

Different dimensions of limerence are predictable by key psychological constructs. Recent research suggests limerence is best understood as a two-dimensional construct, comprised of both an intense need for attachment and neglect of self or others (Marshall et al., 2025).

Attachment anxiety, imaginative fantasy (i.e., the tendency to daydream), and the need to belong are linked to the need-for-attachment dimension of limerence for those experiencing it. This dimension is also predicted by psychological inflexibility and emotional dependence, obsessive preoccupation, self-conscious anxiety, and idealization (Marshall et al., 2025). The neglect dimension operates similarly, except it is not predicted by attachment orientation or idealization, and is associated with more social anxiety and lower self-esteem.

In a recent development, whereas scholars have noted parallels between limerence and addiction and noted the potential path from limerence to stalking (e.g., Bradbury et al., 2025), there's reason to suggest that limerence can also serve as a coping mechanism in an unfulfilling relational context. Experiencing limerence can be a one-time experience or repeated, short-lived or long (Tennov, 1979), yet the context in which it occurs offers the suggestion that it is the mind's way of addressing an undermet need for belonging and intimacy. The field has much more to learn about limerence as an unusual manifestation of the human attachment system.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam.
  • The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

In a recent development, battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Sources indicate that battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

Recent findings suggest that november’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

#63912. Waymo halts highway operation nationwide after CA DMV pause

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (901 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Waymo halts highway operation nationwide after CA DMV pause

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (901 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.
  • Waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017.
  • The vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.

Waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017. It has now expanded to 15 areas, recently adding another 250 square miles just last month.

The vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas. Since it can operate at any time but only within geofenced areas, this counts as “level 4” autonomy, as compared to the level 2 autonomy available on most consumer vehicles.

It has been revealed that until recently, Waymo only operated on city streets. These are more complex than highways, but lower speed. Accidents are more common on city streets than on highways, but can be more spectacular on highways given the higher speeds involved.

According to recent reports, most driver assist systems have been rolled out gradually, starting with highways, due to this lower complexity. But Waymo started with city streets first, bucking that trend.

The organization started offering rides on highways late last year, but only in limited markets. It had been testing highway operation for several years prior, typically with a driver and with no public ridership.

Recent findings suggest that everything was going pretty well, with Waymo declaring its autonomous vehicles have stopped 841 injuries over the course of their 271 million miles of operation. And in terms of competition, Waymo is far ahead of Tesla’s Robotaxi effort.

But then, the viral internet stepped in. Last week, a video surfaced showing a Waymo trying to pass two police cars who were trying to slow down traffic on I-280 in Northern California. This is one of the main routes through Silicon Valley, and the opening of highway operations drastically reduced ride times in the area.

Industry observers note that the video reveals two police cars behind a construction vehicle, lights on and spread out across the freeway. Then it pans to show a Waymo vehicle moving quickly in the far left lane. One of the officers accelerates and swerves in front of the Waymo vehicle, at which point the Waymo swerves and slows down. (One media citation says that the video seems to have been sped up by the original poster, but we’ve embedded the short local news report on it above).

In a recent development, in response to this, the California DMV contacted Waymo and ordered the firm to pause highway operations while it examines the incident. The order was made on November 11, but wasn’t reported until today.

In a recent development, the DMV cited multiple instances of Waymo vehicles incurring into construction zones, not simply the one viral clip above. It mentioned that previous incidents had occurred and been noted, and corrective actions were implemented, but that the incidents keep happening.

According to recent reports, this is a very rare situation which Waymo handled poorly. Waymo will add this case to their their test suite. They'll probably ask the CHP for their in car videos of other cases and convert those to be additional test cases. Waymo has been very willing to admit when their vehicles make mistakes in rare situations and fix it so that it doesn't happen again.

Waymo's vehicles are compared against perfect driving and Waymo accepts that as an aspirational goal. I note Tesla lacks the confidence in their system to even apply for the California permit to begin autonomous testing.

DMV’s pause will remain until Waymo can demonstrate “effective corrective actions” have been taken.

Sources indicate that while the DMV’s order only applies to California highways, Waymo also paused highway operations in other states. It remains operating on city streets in all coverage areas.

Patch: Waymo emailed us this statement after it saw this article.

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

Letter from the Editor-in-Chief: What a Missed Deadline Taught Me About Switching Off

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (850 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The piece you’re reading was supposed to be filed before I headed out on a long weekend to Italy for my wife’s birthday.
  • Industry observers note that the main problem was I simply ran out of time to write the piece.
  • The other problem and consequence was that I carried a chunk of guilt into the break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I missed a deadline last week. The piece you’re reading was supposed to be filed before I headed out on a long weekend to Italy for my wife’s birthday.

Industry observers note that the main problem was I simply ran out of time to write the piece. An urgent stakeholder ask out of the blue, a couple of unanticipated work fire drills, and a long-standing evening social commitment earlier in the week made for a perfect storm, and something had to give.

The other problem and consequence was that I carried a chunk of guilt into the break.

Industry observers note that it caught up with me at 6 am on the first morning, when I found myself drafting this column in my head. I should have been dozing peacefully. I continued to ruminate on my lengthy to-do list at work deep into day one as we headed from Venice into the Dolomites. My body was in Italy, but my brain was clearly still at my desk.

Switching off, particularly from work, is hard for most of us, and especially in an age of ubiquitous screens and wall-to-wall information competing for our attention. For me, that always-on reality plays a major role in the difficulties I have disconnecting from the daily grind.

In a recent development, I’m fortunate to love my job, and if I’m candid, I probably take a little too much of my identity from it. I hold on tight, and the phone in my pocket is an ever-present enabler.

Sources indicate that A meme that has stuck with me over the years goes something along the lines of being an adult is staring at medium screens all day only to come home and stare at a little screen while a substantial screen is on in the background. The irony is not lost on me that I came across this rather withering take on modern life while scrolling on said little screen.

Recent findings suggest that regardless of the role the screen plays, psychologists who study employee well-being describe what I was missing for the early part of the weekend as “psychological detachment.” A state where you are genuinely able to not think about work while away from it. The science suggests it’s an key thing to work on.

It has been revealed that A 2025 meta-analysis of 32 studies found that vacationing has a strong effect on well-being, and that the effect lasts longer than earlier research suggested. A second, smaller analysis of eight studies points to detaching from work, along with physical activity, as among the most helpful things to do while you’re off. In another study that tracked teachers during a two-week break, exhaustion, anxiety, and low mood all declined, while those who kept ruminating about work recovered less.

Industry observers note that whatever the science indicates, I know that for me the act of stepping away from work and being disciplined about not checking back in while I’m away is critical for my mental health and for staving off burnout. Getting out in nature and hiking or cycling or swimming keeps me present. It resets and recharges my batteries, and it tops up my creativity in a way that I find benefits what I am then able to bring back to the office.

Sources indicate that sure enough, as we drove deeper into the mountains on a crisp, blue-sky day, I could feel the golden autumnal hues and majestic rock formations drawing me in, closer to an elemental feeling of calm and happiness. That sense of equilibrium stayed with me all weekend, and while I’d be lying if I stated my mind didn’t occasionally drift to my desk, it was fleeting, with the knowledge that all the things would be waiting for me when I got back. Just like this piece was.

In a recent development, with Thanksgiving on the horizon, and the holidays coming thick and fast thereafter, I’ll leave you with this bit of hard-earned advice: if your job is deeply entwined with your life and part of who you are, as mine is, time away can sometimes feel like a small act of disloyalty. It isn’t. In fact, it’s probably the most vital thing you can do to remain faithful to your work ethic, and to yourself.

It has been revealed that and if you’ll be working over the holidays, or you’re not working right now, or you don’t have the benefit of someone on hand to carry some of the load for you (shout out to all the Grannies out there), or your vacation looks very different from mine, that’s all okay. Find the pockets where and when you can: an evening, a walk, an hour in front of a screen, or better yet a book, and let work wait. Above all else, be kind to yourself. That’s how you really give yourself a break.

Robin Hough is the Editor-in-Chief of Healthline, and in addition to this regular Letter from the Editor column, he can be found every other Wednesday in our Healthline Wellness Wire newsletter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if your domicile happens to exist, say, under a large boulder, you might not have heard that Grand Theft Auto VI is finally arriving at the stroke of midnight on November 19. Those of us who watch television, browse the web, scroll social media, listen to the radio, read the newspaper, flip through magazines, or consume outside info in any way are well aware of the video game, however. It’s the latest installment of the immensely popular “Grand Theft Auto” series, which combines a (surprisingly deep) vein of car culture with an immersive open world full of theft, fighting, drugs, and other violent delights.

Industry observers note that while the previous games came out on a semi-regular schedule of one every few years, it’s been 13 trips ‘round the sun since the last one hit stores. (GTA VI’s development has been so delayed, it even inspired a meme.) Suffice it to say, there’s a lot of pent-up anticipation—even enough to spark half-founded panic headlines about millions of people around the world call in sick to play. But there’s another report that puts a bit more solid of a figure on the excitement around the game. According to digital analysis firm SensorTower, GTA VI has already racked up $1.65 billion in pre-sales ahead of its launch.

That correlates to a little over 17 million orders for the game so far, according to the report, with 75 percent of pre-sales going for the PlayStation 5 version and the other 25 percent for Xbox Series X|S consoles. The chart reveals a fairly typical exponential curve growth over the last five months since pre-sales kicked off: a long period of incremental gains, followed by rapid acceleration in the last few weeks.

And GTA VI-based revenue seems likely to keep coming in to creator Rockstar Games’s coffers at quite a clip, considering initial reviews for the game have been stellar so far. While it may not be your typical automotive-themed driving game, the latest release seems all but sure to guarantee Grand Theft Auto remains a serious part of car culture for some time to come.

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Industry observers note that black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Industry observers note that coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios states the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

In a recent development, the game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

According to recent reports, though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

According to recent reports, so far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai revealed the production-ready Neira EV for the first time, a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV set to launch in Indonesia on November 20.

After introducing the Neira Concept at the 2026 Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show (GIIAS) in July, Hyundai is gearing up to open pre-orders on November 20.

The Neira is a pretty “massive” deal as Hyundai’s first locally produced seven-seat electric SUV in Indonesia.

Ahead of its official debut on Friday at GAIKINDO Auto Week (GAW) 2026, Hyundai offered a closer look at the upcoming Neira.

According to recent reports, the electric SUV is essentially a Hyundai-badged version of the Kia Carens Clavis EV that introduced last year. Aside from the Hyundai logos, a few minor tweaks to the front and rear ends, and fresh wheels and headlights, it’s a near replica.

Inside, both are equipped with dual 12.3″ instrument display and center navigation screens, plus an added climate control panel.

Hyundai didn’t reveal battery or powertrain specs, but the Neira is expected to use the same 42 kWh and 51.4 kWh battery packs as the Carens Clavis EV. The former offers an MIDC range of up to 251 mi (404 km), while the latter has up to 304 mi (490 km) on a single charge.

Both batteries can be charged from 10% to 80% in around 39 minutes using a 100 kW DC fast charger.

The Kia Carens Clavis is 4,550 mm long, 1,800 mm wide, and 1,708 mm tall, with a 2,780 mm wheelbase, so Hyundai’s Neira will likely be about the same size, if not slightly bigger.

Hyundai said the Neira has four key advantages: A higher ground clearance, Hyundai Bluelink connectivity tech, a Blind-spot View Monitor (BVM), and easy third-row access.

A post shared by Hyundai Motors Indonesia (@hyundaimotorindonesia).

Ahead of its upcoming launch, Hyundai is taking the electric 7-seater on a trip to prove its capabilities, going from Kilometer Nol in Banda Aceh to Banda Neira, which is about 4,000 kilometers (about 2,500 miles).

While Hyundai may export the Neira EV to overseas markets like India, don’t expect it to reach the US.

Hyundai already sells a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, which is built at Hyundai’s Metaplant in Georgia.

#63905. Latest Update: Tested: 2027 Subaru Forester Wilderness Hybrid Is a Fuel-Economy-Hero Of a Soft-Roader

Latest Update: Tested: 2027 Subaru Forester Wilderness Hybrid Is a Fuel-Economy-Hero Of a Soft-Roader

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability.
  • Sources indicate that naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim.
  • Our expert editors test every vehicle we review.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability. So it should be no surprise that its Wilderness line of slightly more capable crossovers has been a hit. So, too, has Subaru’s integration of hybrid systems, in an era when buyers of volume cars such as the Forester are happy to get their hands on anything that means greater efficiency.

Sources indicate that naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim. The recipe seems like a sales hit waiting to happen, but is it worth the extra complexity?

Our expert editors test every vehicle we review. Read more about how we test and review cars here.

Subaru finally brought a hybrid powertrain to the Forester for the 2025 model year. A fresh Wilderness was introduced a few months later, but it lacked the gas-electric system available on the basic car. The Forester Wilderness Hybrid combines the two, allowing Subaru to offer a system peak of 194 horsepower from a 2.5-liter flat-four and a 1-kWh battery pack.

EPA-estimated fuel economy is down slightly from the basic Forester Hybrid, but the 33 mpg city and 29 mpg highway are still both solid numbers for a crossover with 9.3 inches of ground clearance and Yokohama Geolander all-terrain tires. For most buyers, that improvement alone should justify the price, which is $1000 more than the basic Forester Wilderness.

Powertrain: 2.5-liter Atkinson-cycle flat-four, lithium-ion hydride battery pack.

Power: 194 hp @ 5600 rpm (peak system output).

Transmission: continuously variable automatic, all-wheel drive.

EPA mpg: 33 city, 29 highway, 31 combined.

It has been revealed that befitting the Wilderness Hybrid’s soft-roader credentials, the media drive took place on the dirt, grass, and gravel roads of a private ranch. While this made for beautiful scenery, it did little to showcase what the car could do as a daily driver or challenge its off-road capabilities.

Recent findings suggest that those capabilities did impress on a more technical off-roading course that Subaru built for the event, although that comes with the caveat that the firm presumably built the course with the car’s limits in mind. Even though this is ultimately still a relatively conventional crossover with nothing like the articulation of a more extreme off-roader, the all-terrain tires were capable of handling substantial ruts and steep hill descents.

Sources indicate that approach, break-over, and departure angles of 23.5, 20.6, and 25.5 degrees, respectively, are identical to the nonhybrid Forester Wilderness. This hybrid crossover has the clearance to get over obstacles a car camper or kayaker might find on the trail to their favorite outdoor-recreation spot. The biggest frustration here was the low resolution of the X-Drive off-road menus built into the infotainment screens, a feature that felt behind the respectable capabilities of the crossover itself.

While the off-road performance is what sets the Wilderness apart from its more pedestrian Forester Hybrid brethren, limited on-road testing suggests that the car feels similar in everyday situations. Given the all-terrain tires, that’s a solid achievement, even if the end result is still relative mediocrity. This Forester is no performance car, and anyone who might have been expecting a canyon carver will instead have to make do with relaxed acceleration and a frustrating continuously variable automatic transmission.

Industry observers note that the Forester is a tentpole for Subaru because it combines the basic compact-crossover shape today’s buyers want with some degree of utility in all forms. The Wilderness goes one step further in providing even more capability, but its day-to-day strength will be how little it sacrifices to do that.

Recent findings suggest that the Forester Wilderness Hybrid drops 5 mpg of efficiency in the city in comparison to the standard Forester Hybrid, for 33 mpg. The basic Forester Wilderness, by contrast, gets just 24 mpg in the city. The hybrid remains relatively comfortable and quiet on the road too, which is great news for buyers who do not want to hear harsh noises from all-terrain tires and the unique drone of a Subaru boxer engine all day.

According to recent reports, still, the Wilderness line is differentiated by its capabilities. Buyers looking for a soft-roader do expect to use the car on a trail every so often, which makes the Wilderness Hybrid’s lack of a spare tire a major matter. Since components of the hybrid system are packed where a spare would go on a normal Wilderness, buyers of this car will either have to find another way to carry a fifth tire or contend with the reality that a flat could derail their outdoor adventures in a worse way than the same problem would in the nonhybrid model.

Industry observers note that that missing spare tire is one of two major drawbacks for the Wilderness Hybrid. The other is the towing capacity, down from 3500 pounds to just 1500. Both of these are serious limitations for buyers who have certain use cases in mind for their soft-roader, but neither is necessarily a problem for the average buyer. The price difference is not negligible, but fuel savings should cover the difference in cost within a few years. For most buyers, that makes the Hybrid the obvious choice.

Sources indicate that buyers looking at other hybrid soft-roaders could also consider the fresh Toyota RAV4 Woodland and the Honda CR-V Trailsport. The Subaru is the only one of the three hybrids with conventional full-time all-wheel drive, although that specific differentiator is not necessarily a game changer for buyers who will be spending most of their time on the street. For those who do need to venture a little further a little more often, though, the Forester Hybrid Wilderness seems like the strongest choice.

Subaru’s Wilderness models are sold with synthetic StarTex interiors meant to be easily cleaned, and this particular vehicle even includes a synthetic steering-wheel cover in lieu of the usual leather. This is a small detail for most, but it does mean that the cabin is entirely vegan. For some very specific buyers, however, that one detail could make all the difference.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hailey Bieber is sharing her experience with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a condition she claims has fueled her growing interest in women’s health research.
  • The Rhode Beauty founder recently announced a $5 million, three-year partnership with the Foundation for Women’s Health in an interview with Women’s Wear Daily (WWD).
  • “As a woman, I feel frustrated by the lack of research, the lack of awareness, the lack of certain conversation around it,” Bieber told WWD.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hailey Bieber is sharing her experience with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a condition she claims has fueled her growing interest in women’s health research.

The Rhode Beauty founder recently announced a $5 million, three-year partnership with the Foundation for Women’s Health in an interview with Women’s Wear Daily (WWD).

“As a woman, I feel frustrated by the lack of research, the lack of awareness, the lack of certain conversation around it,” Bieber told WWD.

Motherhood has also shaped her perspective. Bieber welcomed her son, Jack Blues, with her husband, Justin Bieber, in 2024, describing the experience as a “really intense and special journey.”.

She also shared that she “struggled” with PMDD after giving birth, noting that there’s “not a lot of conversation or research around it.”.

“When we can identify with each other and have conversations relating to each other and talking about the things we’re dealing with and struggling with, I do think it makes it feel like less of a lonely journey,” Bieber said.

PMDD is a complexcondition that causes severe physical and psychological symptoms that typically occur in the days or weeks leading up to menstruation.

“What distinguishes PMDD from the more common PMS (premenstrual syndrome) is the severity of the symptoms and how significantly they can interfere with daily functioning,” Sari Eitches, MD, dual board certified physician and medical advisor to Terra Mare, told Healthline.

“Another defining feature is the timing: symptoms typically worsen in the week or two before a period, resolve within a few days after menstruation begins, and are minimal or absent during the rest of the cycle,” she mentioned.

Eitches also noted that PMDD is a chronic condition that can affect women at any stage of their reproductive lives, from adolescence through perimenopause, as long as they are having menstrual cycles.

“It is caused by a sensitivity to cyclic hormonal and neurotransmitter fluctuations, so [it] can occur in anyone with a menstrual cycle, though stages of hormonal fluctuation- including postpartum, weaning breastfeeding, and perimenopause- can be a trigger,” she added.

According to research published in 2024, approximately 1.6% of women and girls meet the strict diagnostic criteria for PMDD, equivalent to an estimated 31 million people worldwide.

A higher percentage of 3.2% have a provisional diagnosis, meaning a healthcare professional may believe a person has PMDD, but symptoms have not been measured for a sustained amount of time to meet the criteria for a confirmed diagnosis.

Eitches said that women with a personal or family history of depression or anxiety may be more prone to developing PMDD, as are women with a family history of PMDD itself.

“PMDD is understood to be caused by a combination of heritable biological sensitivities and environmental triggers. These can include a history of trauma, chronic stress, and other chronic medical conditions,” she noted.

Eitches also said that you should consider seeing a doctor if your symptoms are severe enough that they’re interfering with your ability to go to work or school, maintain your relationships, or participate in your life in the same way that you do during the other weeks of the month.

Sources indicate that to diagnose PMDD, a healthcare professional will review your medical history and symptoms and may perform a physical exam. They will typically ask you to track your symptoms over at least two menstrual cycles.

A PMDD diagnosis generally requires at least five symptoms, including at least one mood-related symptom, that occur before menstruation, improve shortly after a period begins, and significantly interfere with daily life.

The symptoms of PMDD may include:.

Treatment options for PMDD include prescription medications and over-the-counter treatments that may help relieve certain symptoms, such as:.

Eitches noted that cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can also help manage symptoms.

Lifestyle changes may also help manage PMDD symptoms, including practicing relaxation techniques, eating a balanced diet, limiting sugary and salty foods, and getting regular physical activity.

Eitches noted that getting enough high quality sleep and resting on a consistent schedule is also key.

“I also recommend focusing on a whole-foods-based diet, limiting added sugar and caffeine, and avoiding cigarette smoking,” she said.

#63903. Breaking: 5 Evidence-Based Treatments for Borderline Personality Disorder

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1037 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: 5 Evidence-Based Treatments for Borderline Personality Disorder

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • It has been revealed that for a long time, borderline personality disorder (BPD) was considered one of the most difficult mental health conditions to treat.
  • Recent findings suggest that fortunately, decades of research have demonstrated otherwise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

It has been revealed that for a long time, borderline personality disorder (BPD) was considered one of the most difficult mental health conditions to treat. Some therapists even believed that people with BPD couldn't get better.

Recent findings suggest that fortunately, decades of research have demonstrated otherwise. Today, several treatments can help people with BPD manage intense emotions, build healthier relationships, and reduce impulsive behaviors.

Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) is probably the best known, but it's not the only option. Here are five approaches worth considering if you're looking for care for yourself or a loved one.

Developed by psychologist Marsha Linehan, DBT was the first treatment for BPD to demonstrate effectiveness in a randomized clinical trial.

It has been revealed that the results were incredibly promising. Among chronically suicidal women with BPD, those receiving DBT engaged in less self-harm, had fewer psychiatric hospitalizations, and were more likely to stay in treatment than those receiving usual care.

Recent findings suggest that since then, DBT has been evaluated in dozens of randomized clinical trials. Its strongest evidence is for reducing suicidal and self-injurious behaviors, although promising findings extend to substance use, eating disorders, and depression.

DBT is based on the idea that people with BPD experience emotions intensely and may rely on coping strategies that provide temporary relief but create problems in the long run.

According to the treatment manual, comprehensive (full model) DBT programs include several components: weekly individual therapy, weekly skills group, and between-session phone coaching. In individual therapy, it is common to review difficulties that came up during the week and explore alternative responses. In skills group, patients receive didactic (class-like) instruction in four skill areas: mindfulness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness. Between-session phone coaching helps people apply these skills when they need them most.

In a recent development, initially, Marsha Linehan recommended that people with BPD make a year-long commitment to their DBT program. However, many DBT programs now offer care for shorter durations (e.g., 6 months).

Developed by psychologist Peter Fonagy and psychiatrist Anthony Bateman, MBT has demonstrated improvements in BPD symptoms, self-harm, and interpersonal functioning in randomized clinical trials.

MBT focuses on improving mentalizing, our ability to understand our own thoughts and feelings and those of others. Rather than explicitly teaching coping skills, as in DBT, therapists help patients strengthen this ability through interactions during therapy.

For example, imagine leaving a session convinced your therapist was annoyed with you. Rather than simply reassuring you, an MBT therapist might explore what happened and what each of you might have been thinking or feeling.

The therapeutic relationship becomes a place to practice navigating emotionally charged interactions. Treatment typically includes weekly individual and group sessions over 12–18 months.

Developed by psychiatrist Otto Kernberg and colleagues, TFP has demonstrated improvements in BPD symptoms and interpersonal functioning in randomized clinical trials.

Like MBT, TFP focuses on relationships rather than teaching specific coping skills. However, TFP emphasizes difficulties integrating positive and negative perceptions of ourselves and others.

Sources indicate that for example, someone with BPD might see their partner as loving and trustworthy one moment, but cruel and uncaring after a disagreement. TFP helps patients recognize that positive and negative qualities can exist in the same person.

Treatment typically involves twice-weekly individual sessions lasting a year or longer.

Developed by psychiatrist John Gunderson, GPM takes a different approach; the goal is to make effective BPD treatment accessible through generalist mental health clinicians.

Rather than requiring extensive training in specialized psychotherapy, GPM provides a practical framework for understanding BPD, managing crises, and improving everyday functioning.

It has been revealed that particular attention is given to relationships, work, school, and other meaningful activities. Treatment typically involves weekly appointments, with flexibility based on patients' needs.

Importantly, a randomized clinical trial comparing general psychiatric management with DBT found substantial improvements in both groups, including reductions in suicidal and self-injurious behaviors.

This work challenged the assumption that effective BPD treatment necessarily requires a highly specialized, intensive program.

BPD Compass is a newer cognitive-behavioral treatment my colleagues and I developed to make evidence-based BPD care more efficient and accessible.

According to recent reports, we were intrigued that existing treatments all produce meaningful improvements, with no single approach consistently outperforming the others. This suggests that each addresses something vital, whether that's emotion regulation (DBT), relationships (MBT, TFP), or building a meaningful life (GPM).

According to recent reports, yet many patients continue experiencing symptoms after treatment. We wondered whether nonresponse might reflect a mismatch between patients' difficulties and the treatment they receive.

We designed BPD Compass to address three broad vulnerabilities associated with BPD: emotion dysregulation, relationship difficulties, and impulsivity. In our clinical trials, treatment begins with an assessment to identify which patterns are driving a particular patient's symptoms, followed by an individualized proposal emphasizing the most relevant modules.

BPD Compass takes 18 sessions, considerably shorter than many established BPD treatments. Like GPM, it was designed for generalist clinicians without requiring extensive specialized training.

In an initial randomized clinical trial, participants receiving BPD Compass indicated large improvements in BPD symptoms. Subsequent research also documented improvements in emotional, relational, and impulsive functioning, as well as symptoms of co-occurring conditions.

Recent findings suggest that BPD is an incredibly heterogeneous condition. Some people experience frequent suicidal crises and need intensive, long-term support. Others may make meaningful progress with a shorter intervention.

As a BPD treatment developer, my goal isn't to replace existing treatments. It's to expand the options available. Not everyone with BPD needs year-long therapy, and we should have effective, personalized alternatives for those who don't.

Ultimately, the best treatment is one that addresses your difficulties, provides the support you need, and is accessible enough for you to receive it.

It has been revealed that if you or someone you love is contemplating suicide, seek help immediately. For help 24/7, dial 988 for the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, or reach out to the Crisis Text Line by texting TALK to 741741. To find a therapist near you, visit the Psychology Today Therapy Directory.

Iceland’s first wind farm comes with a water-saving bonus

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1314 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.
  • Vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads.
  • It has been revealed that landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power firm, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.

Vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads. And Iceland’s windiest months coincide with the time of year when less water flows into its reservoirs.

It has been revealed that landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power firm, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026. The first 14 turbines are online; another 14 will be installed in a second phase, and the entire wind farm is expected to be operating by the end of 2027.

Recent findings suggest that once complete, Vaðölduver will have 120 megawatts (MW) of capacity. When I met with the folks at Landsvirkjun in Reykjavik last month, they told me that’s enough to power the equivalent of 90,000 Icelandic households. Vaðalda’s electricity feeds into the grid and is sold through power purchase agreements.

Vaðölduver sits on a lava-and-sand plain east of the Þjórsá River, south of Sultartangi Dam. Landsvirkjun already operates seven hydropower stations in the surrounding Þjórsá and Tungnaá region.

The wind farm was sited in this region of Iceland because the seasons line up nicely.

In a recent development, the winds are strongest in winter, when inflows into hydropower reservoirs can be low. In summer, wind speeds tend to drop, but glacial melt increases water availability for the hydropower system.

In a recent development, when the wind turbines are generating plenty of electricity, Landsvirkjun can ease off hydropower and leave more water in its reservoirs. When the wind drops, hydropower can pick up more of the demand.

That gives the utility more control over when it uses its stored water and helps that water go further.

It has been revealed that german wind turbine maker Enercon manufactured Vaðölduver’s turbines. The project also includes a service and maintenance agreement with Enercon.

Industry observers note that landsvirkjun had a decade of experience operating pilot wind turbines before building Vaðölduver. One big thing they learned: They didn’t need tall towers to find plenty of wind.

There’s little vegetation or other surface obstructions across this unique, exposed landscape. That allows the turbines to capture productive winds closer to the ground than they could at a more wooded or sheltered location.

“Lower” is relative, of course. The turbines still reach 150 meters (492 feet) at their highest blade tip.

The wind farm covers 17.1 square kilometers (6.6 square miles). Twenty-five turbines are rated at 4.26 MW each, and the remaining three at 4.5 MW. Landsvirkjun’s presentation puts annual generation at 440 GWh and lists a P50 net efficiency figure of 43%, which is considered strong for onshore wind.

Industry observers note that the ability to tap into existing infrastructure was a major factor in Landsvirkjun’s site selection. Where a wind farm goes affects its cost, its environmental footprint, and the people who live nearby.

Landsvirkjun also identifies active engagement with communities and other stakeholders as essential to building wind projects. At Vaðölduver, the immediate task is to finish the remaining 14 turbines while the first phase completes its trial runs.

It has been revealed that the company sees wind as a potential third pillar of Iceland’s electricity supply alongside hydropower and geothermal. Vaðölduver shows how those resources can work together, with wind adding generation while helping conserve stored water.

It has been revealed that iceland is a world leader in clean energy. It generates nearly 100% of its electricity from renewable sources, combining hydropower fueled by glacial runoff and rivers (around 70%) and geothermal energy (around 30%).

Over 90% of Icelandic households use direct geothermal hot water for space heating and hot water, while the remaining homes use renewable electricity.

But it’s got the same grid capacity challenges as every other country. Adding wind – and anything else that uses power – means paying close attention to what the grid can handle. Iceland has an isolated transmission system, so maintaining stability and ensuring sufficient capacity are increasingly important as the country develops more projects.

In a recent development, while in Reykjavik, I met with the Minister of the Environment, Energy and Climate, Jóhann Páll Jóhannsson, who told me that the Icelandic grid’s capacity is expected to grow from 20 TWh to 24-25 TWh within a decade. Jóhannsson also said that he is pro-data center and that investors are keen to establish more of them in the country.

In a recent development, when I asked Jóhannsson and his team, as well as the teams at Landsvirkjun and publicly owned ON Power, Iceland’s second-largest electricity generator and largest EV charger network, about grid expansion plans to handle that pipeline, they all said that legislative reforms were being passed to speed up energy permitting processes. There is also financing in place to grow the grid. The physical transmission network is being expanded, but the process is slow because NIMBYism is creating bottlenecks.

In learning about fresh and completed Icelandic power projects during my visit, it was apparent that the companies in the power and geothermal heat sector regularly collaborate on projects – everyone brings their expertise to the table and works for the common good (yes, really).

But what was striking in discussions about grid expansion was that there seemed to be no intends to pitch in with the Icelandic transmission system operator (TSO), Landsnet hf. It seemed that the plan was to let the TSO come up with the solutions on its own. At most, Jóhannsson’s team noted its legislative reform “opened the door” to possible grid innovations.

When I asked the Landsvirkjun team whether they were considering working with the TSO on distributed energy resource (DER) projects like virtual power plants and onsite battery storage for its heavy-industry clients, which make up 80% of its business, they stated they hadn’t considered it.

It has been revealed that I often wonder why Quebec hasn't followed this strategy. They have huge dams with world-leading power connections, and one of the problem they are facing is a lack of water to refill those dams, due to several years of relative drought. I know it costs a lot to build wind power up north, but siting a project there would re-use their massive investment in power lines. The dams would act as gigantic batteries, because they wouldn't need to drain their reservoirs when the wind is blowing.

Iceland has earned its reputation as a clean energy leader. Bringing that same collaborative and creative approach to expanding its grid would help it keep setting an example for the rest of the world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, taking a vintage muscle car and swapping in modern components to make it run better or add power is a story as old as, well, the LS2 V-8. Vintage Modern’s new Fastback Mustang turns that formula upside down—by swapping old-school body parts onto a modern S650-generation Mustang GT. But the Vintage Modern Fastback, officially revealed on Wednesday at Retromobile New York, is more than just a body kit.

For starters, Ford’s standard 5.0-liter V-8 is mated here to a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger for a total output of 840 horsepower and 615 lb-ft of torque. Prospective buyers can choose between a six-speed manual transmission with rev matching or a 10-speed automatic with steering-wheel-mounted paddle shifters. Other high-end Mustang features like active-valve performance exhaust with four sound modes, MagneRide adaptive suspension, six selectable drive modes, and Brembo performance brakes are also standard fare.

Sources indicate that “The Vintage Fastback is a car we’ve always wanted to build. We’ve blended classic-inspired design with modern safety, technology, and performance,” said Chau Nguyen, founder and CEO of Vintage Modern. “This is what Vintage Modern was created to do.”.

According to recent reports, even though the bones of the Fastback are from a current-generation Mustang, the heavily modified vehicle still underwent crash testing to meet applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. This retro-inspired Mustang features eight airbags, crumple zones, side-impact beams, electronic stability control, traction control, and anti-lock brakes. That’s more than most restomod Mustang owners can say.

In a recent development, most of the custom body panels, including the functional hood scoop, are carbon fiber; the only obviously metal pieces are the billet-aluminum grille, door handles, mirrors, and twin auxiliary driving lights. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning.
  • Sources indicate that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned. Of course, there was a convertible version of the Temerario coming. And on Wednesday, November 18, the automaker unveiled it for the first time—and it is called, of course, the Temerario Spyder.

Formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning. The Temerario was designed with the Spyder always in mind; as such, there’s space enough behind the two seats for the new power folding hardtop to snick down inside almost perfectly vertically. The firewall between the cockpit and the mid-mounted, twin-turbocharged V-8 doesn’t change its location, but the space behind the seats is utilized differently.

Sources indicate that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California. This is the first Lambo to use a retractable hardtop.

Sources indicate that 10 electric actuators split the two-piece top, open a hatch behind the seats, and move the structure down into its narrow warren. It’s a fully electric system, so there are no hydraulic lines to split open. Lamborghini indicates the power top adds about 100 kilograms (220 pounds) to the Temerario’s mass, but that’s all at the center of the car, so that front-to-rear weight balance is maintained. With the roof open, says the maker, the center of gravity drops about three millimeters from where it is when closed.

The hardtop should also produce close to a coupe-like experience when it is closed.“We reinforce the structure of the Spyder,” explains Fermin Soneira, Lambo’s chief technical officer, about the Temerario Spyder’s aluminum space frame. “So, for example, we use some hydroformed pieces in place of castings at some points.”.

Industry observers note that the Temerario Spyder takes the market position that was once held by the Huracan Spyder, and Lamborghini claims this new architecture is six percent stiffer in torsional rigidity and nine percent up in dynamic bending stiffness than that car. If all that stiff isn’t stiffy enough, there’s also a six percent increase in dynamic torsional rigidity. So, it’s a super-stiffy thing.

The increase in weight means the suspension has been slightly tweaked to deal with it. “If you change the weight, you have to change the spring rate to keep the same natural frequency,” says Soneira. “In this case, it was not about leaving everything the same, but also about increasing comfort in the ‘Strada’ drive mode. Still, if you go to the Hockenheimring, there’s less than a one second per lap difference between the coupe and the Spyder.”.

Top up or down, the most spectacular element of every Temerario is the flat-plane crank, 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 that’s incorporated into the hybrid all-wheel drive powertrain. With a lightweight reciprocating assembly that includes titanium connecting rods, the engine will spin to a thrilling 10,000-rpm redline. “We have a upcoming calibration of the engine sound,” adds Soneira, “so you end up with a slightly different voice than in the coupe. The target is always ‘let’s keep improving,’ so these changes will come to the coupe too.”.

In a recent development, combined with three electric motors, the Temerario has 907 horsepower aboard—and despite all the electronic hickey-doos, it still stirs up and blasts like a true supercar. That’s not likely to change with the Spyder.

Production of the Spyder will be done in batches along the regular Temerario assembly line, with the first saleable models due to be completed as this is published. Lamborghini expects about 50 percent of Temerario production to be Spyders. Prices haven’t been revealed, but should start around $400,000 and go up from there only limited by the buyer’s imagination and wallet.

Does Menopausal Hormone Therapy Lower Dementia Risk? Timing and Genetics May Hold the Answer

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women who have longer reproductive life spans or use menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) may have better brain health as they age, according to a new study.
  • The research, published November 4 in Neurology, found that longer lifetime exposure to estrogen was associated with fewer signs of damage to small blood vessels in the brain.
  • The findings could offer fresh insights into the relationship between estrogen and brain aging, particularly as women account for approximately two-thirds of Alzheimer’s disease cases worldwide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women who have longer reproductive life spans or use menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) may have better brain health as they age, according to a new study.

The research, published November 4 in Neurology, found that longer lifetime exposure to estrogen was associated with fewer signs of damage to small blood vessels in the brain.

The findings could offer fresh insights into the relationship between estrogen and brain aging, particularly as women account for approximately two-thirds of Alzheimer’s disease cases worldwide.

Researchers also found that certain associations between hormone therapy and brain health differed depending on whether women carried a genetic variant associated with an increased risk of Alzheimer’s disease.

In a recent development, however, the relationship between estrogen and brain health is complex. While the findings suggest that longer estrogen exposure may be associated with healthier brain aging, they do not establish that hormone therapy can prevent Alzheimer’s disease or dementia.

The researchers drew data from the Gothenburg H70-1944 Birth Cohort, a longitudinal study of 1,203 individuals born in 1944 who resided in Gothenburg, Sweden.

The final cohort included 352 cisgender women, with an average age of 70, who had no neurological disorders and reliable self-reported data on their estrogen exposure.

In a recent development, individual estrogen exposure was measured through structured interviews. It included:.

The researchers used this information as a proxy for lifetime estrogen exposure, though the study didn’t measure actual hormone levels.

Participants were also given a brain MRI at baseline and then again at a 5-year follow-up.

The researchers found that those with a longer reproductive span had a lower risk of small vessel disease (SVD). Participants with a longer reproductive life span had an 8% lower risk of having two or more signs of SVD. However, later menopause, rather than earlier menstruation, appeared to be the main driver of this association.

Those who used MHT also tended to have fewer signs of SVD and better microstructural integrity in the white matter.

In individuals who carried the APOE-ε4 variant, which increases a person’s risk of Alzheimer’s disease, MHT was associated with greater cortical thickness in brain regions vulnerable to Alzheimer’s disease. However, there was no association for those without this variant.

The researchers noted that longer estrogen exposure was associated with stable cortical thickness and white matter trajectories over time.

Dung Trinh, MD, internist at MemorialCare Medical Group and Chief Medical Officer of Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that estrogen has several important effects on the brain that may help support cognitive health.

It influences communication between brain cells, supports the brain’s ability to use glucose for energy, helps regulate neurotransmitters, and plays a role in maintaining healthy blood vessels and reducing inflammation and oxidative stress.

Sources indicate that “As estrogen levels decline during menopause, some of these protective effects may diminish. Replacing estrogen closer to the menopause transition could potentially help preserve some of these functions during a vulnerable period for brain health,” he said. “While these findings are encouraging, MHT has not been proven to prevent Alzheimer’s disease or dementia.”.

Sherry Ross, MD, board certified OB/GYN and Women’s Health Expert at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who also wasn’t involved in the study, agreed and noted, “Starting menopausal hormone therapy earlier in the menopause transition may help minimize some changes by supporting the brain during this period of hormonal fluctuation.”.

“There is growing interest in whether early estrogen therapy may also help reduce the long-term risk of Alzheimer’s disease, although more research is needed before we can establish that benefit,” she added.

Ross told Healthline that this research reinforces the importance of recognizing menopause as more than a reproductive or hormonal transition.

“We know that women are disproportionately affected by dementia and Alzheimer’s disease, and some women experience noticeable cognitive changes beginning in perimenopause,” she said. “If future research confirms that starting hormone therapy earlier can help protect long-term cognitive health, it could influence how we approach menopause treatment and encourage more proactive conversations between women and their healthcare providers.”.

“The goal should be to individualize treatment based on a woman’s symptoms, medical history, and overall health rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach,” Ross added.

Trinh agreed that an individualized approach to menopause management is notable.

According to recent reports, “This does not mean that every woman should start hormone therapy to prevent dementia. Instead, it highlights the importance of understanding which women might benefit, when treatment should begin, and which formulations are most appropriate,” he said. “Factors such as age, time since menopause, cardiovascular risk, metabolic health, family history, and potentially genetic factors may all help guide future recommendations.”.

“We still need stronger clinical evidence before changing current prescribing guidelines specifically for dementia prevention,” Trinh added.
